_comment: Evidence notes (PLAN 7.3, enriched). unlock_type: 'threshold' (lexicon_size >= unlock_value), 'topic' (topic_signal == unlock_value), or 'empathy' (state.empathy >= unlock_value; raised when the detective asks caring/personal questions). 'act' = earliest act the note can appear. 'found' = how it surfaced in the investigation (no spoilers). 'hint' = {tone_id, text} nudging a tone's meaning, surfaced in the lexicon once that tone is heard. 'summary' = the fragment this note contributes to the Her Story tab; 'order' sequences the assembled narrative. 'body' is the artifact text; 'design' is a render hint.

notes.title: Text thread — 11:43pm
notes.found: Pulled from her phone — the most-read thread on the device.

hint.text: She keeps writing 'i am here' — listen for how she names herself.

notes.summary: She and R were together, but in her last weeks she had gone quiet; he could feel her slipping away and didn't understand why.
notes.design: Screenshot of a phone messaging app, dark bubbles. Timestamp 11:43pm. Read first as a cold breakup; designed to re-read after the twist.
notes.body:
R  ·  11:43pm

R: you've been quiet all week
R: did i do something
Lily: no
R: then talk to me. please
Lily: i'm just tired
R: you're always tired lately
Lily: i know
Lily: i'm sorry
R: i don't want sorry. i want you to be here
Lily: i am here
R: not really

[read 11:51pm]

notes.title: Sketchbook — figure study
notes.found: Found open on her desk, the pencil still resting in the crease.

hint.text: She drew the eyes alive but never the mouth — as if speech itself were the thing missing.

notes.summary: She was an artist before anything else, rendering feeling with a care she rarely allowed herself in words.
notes.design: Pencil figure study. Eyes rendered with extraordinary precision and life. The mouth is absent — not erased, never drawn.
notes.body: A half-finished figure study in soft pencil. The eyes are alive — every lash, the wet light caught in them, rendered with impossible care. The face trails into nothing below them. The mouth was never drawn. In the corner, faint: "come back to this."

notes.title: Award email — Design Symposium
notes.found: Recovered from her inbox during the device review. Still marked unread.
notes.summary: Her work was named a finalist at an international symposium — an email that arrived too late for her to ever open.
notes.design: An email client screenshot. Subject highlighted. Status: UNREAD. Timestamp two days AFTER the accident date (callback in Act III).
notes.body:
From: International Design Symposium <awards@idsymposium.org>
Subject: Congratulations — you are a Finalist
Received: [two days after the incident]   ●  UNREAD

"We are thrilled to inform you that your submission, 'A Held Breath,' has been selected as a finalist in this year's Generative & Mixed-Media category..."

The message was never opened.

notes.title: CS assignment — margin notes
notes.found: Among the printouts in her bag, soft at the edges from being carried everywhere.

hint.text: She wrote about something that 'waits and waits' before it lets go — a holding, a staying in place.

notes.summary: She studied computer science but read it like poetry, finding a held breath and a release inside a recursive function.
notes.design: Scan of a printed CS assignment, dense with handwritten margin notes and tiny drawings. Warm, alive, personal.
notes.body:
Printed lab sheet: 'Assignment 4 — Recursive Structures.' The margins are full. Tiny drawings — a fern, a staircase, a wave. Beside one function, in careful handwriting:

"this function feels like a held breath. it waits and waits and then all at once it lets everything go. i think that's beautiful. (will prof think i'm insane if i write that in the report) (writing it anyway)"

notes.title: Photograph — at her desk
notes.found: Shared by a classmate who had taken it weeks earlier, unprompted, and kept it.

hint.text: Caught mid-laugh — this is the brightness the lighter tone carries.

notes.summary: To the people around her she was vivid and ordinarily alive — beautiful chaos at a crowded desk.
notes.design: Candid photo, someone else's camera. Lily laughing at her desk, beautiful chaos around her. The note that makes the player love her.
notes.body: A candid photo — she didn't know it was being taken. Lily at her desk mid-laugh, head tipped back, hand half-raised as if to wave the camera off. Around her: pinned sketches curling at the corners, three open textbooks, three half-empty mugs, a tangle of cables, a single dried flower taped to the monitor. The room is beautiful chaos. She looks completely, ordinarily alive.

notes.title: Text thread — two days before
notes.found: A later thread on the same phone, dated two days before the incident.

hint.text: Every message here is to the same person — the one she names with a single tone.

notes.summary: Two days before, R was still reaching for her; she answered in one word, then went silent.
notes.design: Second message thread. R is trying hard; Lily answers in one word then goes silent. Player now understands she was pulling away.
notes.body:
R  ·  two days before

R: are you okay?
Lily: yeah
R: can we talk
Lily: soon
R: just tell me what's wrong. whatever it is
R: i'm not going anywhere
Lily: i know
R: ?
R: lily?

[delivered]

notes.title: Hospital intake form
notes.found: Released from the hospital's records after a formal request. The file is incomplete.
notes.summary: A hospital intake bearing her name — unsigned, the status field blacked out, discharge left as N/A.
notes.design: Standard intake form. Admission date smudged/illegible. Status field covered by a thick black redaction bar. Discharge: N/A.
notes.body:
MERCY GENERAL — PATIENT INTAKE

Patient name:  Lily Anne
Date of admission:  [smudged — illegible]
Attending:  ——————
Status:  ████████████████
Discharge date:  N / A

Form incomplete. Filed without signature.

notes.title: Nurse shift log
notes.found: Cross-checked against the ward roster for the week of the incident — twice.
notes.summary: The staff she seemed to remember from the ward appear nowhere on the roster — no record of them at all.
notes.design: Photocopy of the ward shift log for the relevant week. The nurse Lily seemed to reference appears nowhere. No matching name on record.
notes.body:
WARD 4 — SHIFT LOG (week of the incident)

Mon  Okafor / Reyes
Tue  Reyes / Halloran
Wed  Halloran / Brandt
Thu  Brandt / Okafor
Fri  Okafor / Reyes

No entry matches the name. No staff by that name is on the ward roster. Cross-checked twice.

notes.title: Journal page
notes.found: A torn page, recovered folded inside the back cover of her sketchbook.

hint.text: 'it isn't you. it was never you.' — she circles one small, firm word.

notes.summary: On a torn page she rehearsed what she meant to tell R that night: that it was never his fault, and she should have said it weeks ago.
notes.design: Torn page from a small notebook. Handwriting more hurried than usual. What she was going to say to R, written out so she'd get it right.
notes.body:
A torn page, the handwriting faster than usual:

"ok. say it plainly. — it isn't you. it was never you. i need space to become the thing i'm trying to become and i can't do that and be what you need at the same time, not yet. i love you in a way that doesn't fit the shape we made. that's not your fault. i should have said it weeks ago.

tell him tonight. on the walk back. don't write around it this time."

notes.title: Childhood folder — two homes
notes.found: Recovered from a storage box at her father's apartment; her mother kept an identical one.

hint.text: A child's drawing labels two houses and the people in each — reach for a word that means more-than-one, together.

notes.summary: Her parents divorced when she was eleven; she grew up between two homes, learning early how to pack herself away and move on before she could be left.
notes.design: A folder of a child's drawings and a custody calendar. One crayon house labelled 'mum's', another 'dad's', a small figure drawn carefully into both.
notes.body:
A worn folder of childhood drawings, kept in duplicate by both parents.

One page: two crayon houses, far apart on the paper. 'MUM'S' over one, 'DAD'S' over the other, and a small figure drawn carefully into both, holding nothing in either hand.

A school worksheet behind it — 'MY FAMILY' — has one parent quietly erased and redrawn, twice. Clipped to the back: a custody calendar, alternating weeks in two colours, every handover circled.

notes.title: Statement — her friend, M
notes.found: Her closest friend came forward during the investigation and asked to give a statement.

hint.text: M describes how intensely she felt everything — the tone for sensing, for feeling.

notes.summary: To the one friend who knew the whole of it, she seemed worn thin but hopeful — on the edge, finally, of something better.
notes.design: A typed witness statement from a friend, 'M'. Plain, fond, a little broken.
notes.body:
STATEMENT — witness 'M' (friend)

"She felt everything so hard. People thought she was calm but she just hid it well. This last month she was running on nothing — the project, classes, the thing with R she didn't know how to fix.

But she was hopeful. That's the part I can't— she texted me that morning. Said she'd finally figured out what to say to him, that she'd tell him on the walk back and do it properly this time. She used a little smiley.

She was going to be okay. That's what I don't understand."

[statement ends]

notes.title: Voicemail — her mother, three weeks before
notes.found: Retrieved from her phone's saved messages — the last one from her mother, kept but never returned.

hint.text: The message is about distance and leaving unanswered — listen for the tone that moves away.

notes.summary: She had been pulling away from her mother for years — the same quiet retreat R felt was never really about him at all.
notes.design: Transcript of a saved voicemail, timestamp three weeks prior. Warm, tentative, unanswered.
notes.body:
SAVED VOICEMAIL — 'Mum' — three weeks before

"Hi sweetheart. It's me. I know you're busy, you're always busy lately, that's okay. I just — I saw something today that reminded me of you and I wanted to hear your voice.

Call me back when you can. Or don't, if you can't. I just love you. That's all. Okay. Bye. Bye."

Never returned. Saved, not deleted.

notes.title: Counseling referral — folded small
notes.found: Found folded into a tight square in her wallet, behind her student card.

hint.text: Under the 'just tired' she gave everyone, she had named a feeling with a tremor in it.

notes.summary: Beneath the 'just tired' she told everyone, she had begun to struggle — and had just taken the first small step toward asking for help.
notes.design: A campus wellbeing referral slip, appointment dated the week after the incident. Folded many times.
notes.body:
STUDENT WELLBEING — REFERRAL

Name:  Lily Anne
Reason (self-described):  "low mood / exhausted / 'don't feel like myself' — would like to talk to someone"
First appointment:  [the week after the incident]
Status:  NOT ATTENDED

The slip had been folded and refolded until the creases had nearly worn through.

notes.title: Letter to her mother — unsent
notes.found: Tucked into the lining of her sketchbook — unaddressed, the envelope never sealed.

hint.text: She was trying to hold onto something she meant to finally say — a keeping, a remembering.

notes.summary: She was afraid of ending things the way her parents had — in silence and blame — and that fear shaped how she loved R, and how she kept leaving before she could be left.
notes.design: A handwritten letter, never sent, the hand careful and then hurried. To her mother.
notes.body:
(unsent, tucked into the sketchbook lining)

"Mum — I'm sorry I go quiet. I think I learned it from the house. When things got hard, you and dad just went somewhere I couldn't follow, and I taught myself to do the same so it wouldn't hurt as much.

I don't want to end things the way you two did. Not with R, not with you. I keep pulling away from everyone so I can be the one who leaves first. I know that isn't brave. I want to stop.

I'm going to call you. I'm going to tell R the truth, kindly, this time. I just need to be ready. I'll write it all down first so I get it right."

notes.title: Police report — case closed
notes.found: The closed case file, released last of all.
notes.summary: The incident report, case closed: she was found deceased at the scene, at a crossing on library road. No other party involved.
notes.design: Appears differently from all others — placed flat in the center of the board, not pinned. Incident date matches N07 admission date.
notes.body:
INCIDENT REPORT — CASE CLOSED

Name of deceased:  Lily Anne, 19
Date of incident:  [matches admission date]
Location:  pedestrian crossing, library road

Findings:  Deceased at the scene. No other parties involved. No further action.
Personal effects catalogued and returned to family.

Case closed.
